_how_to_edit: The story page, replay map and home hero read this file on every load. Edit it, run `node groundstop/src/build.js`, commit and push to main; no Squarespace edit is needed. Times are hours on an Eastern clock on Nov. 13, 2026 (17.5 = 5:30 p.m.; values past 24 mean Nov. 14). Set lift to null while the stop is in effect.
headline_status: The ground stop is still in effect, and the FAA is releasing some flights as centers recover
cause: Telecommunications outage at air traffic control
moments: A Friday afternoon, with flights departing on schedule across the country.
Flights bound for Chicago O’Hare are stopped over communications problems, and Midway follows three minutes later.
Nationwide ground stop. More than 3,100 flights already in the air are allowed to continue to their destinations.
The transportation secretary says a communication issue is affecting air route traffic control centers.
The FAA advisory now runs to 11:30 p.m. Eastern, and no end time is confirmed.
The FAA says a temporary telecommunications outage caused the stop, and officials say they see no sign of an attack.
The FAA says the stop remains in effect and that flights will be released as each en route center recovers.
Fox Weather counts 598 commercial flights still in the air, down from more than 3,100 when the stop began.
The stop is in its fourth hour, and CNN reports that officials have no timeline for resolving it.
facts: Eastern start time, the only one of the three stops to begin after noon
flights in the air when the stop began, allowed to finish their trips
flights delayed by 6:30 p.m. Eastern, with more than 2,500 canceled, according to Fox Weather
unknown: What is not known. The FAA blames a temporary telecommunications outage but has not said what caused the outage or when all departures will resume. An airline source told CNN the problem began with network routers and spread nationwide, which the FAA has not confirmed. This replay ends at 7:06 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, the last time we checked, with the stop still in effect and some flights being released one at a time. Three days earlier, on Nov. 10, the agency expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. No official has connected the tool to the stop, and no reporting so far shows a link.
status_html: As of 7:06 p.m. Eastern on Friday the stop was still in effect, 3 hours and 12 minutes after it began, and CNN reported that officials had no timeline for resolving it. At about 6 p.m. the FAA said flights would be allowed to depart as each en route center recovers, in coordination with its command center, and some international departures from Boston and Pacific-bound departures from San Francisco have been released one at a time. Fox Weather counted more than 10,500 delays and more than 2,500 cancellations by 6:30 p.m., up from 10,494 delays and 1,913 cancellations at 6:04 p.m. The same count showed 598 commercial flights still in the air at 6:30 p.m., about one-fifth of the more than 3,100 that were airborne when the stop began.
compare_html: Friday's stop passed the length of the entire 2023 stop at about 5:24 p.m. and had run 192 minutes by 7:06 p.m., more than twice the roughly 90 minutes of 2023. It also began late on a Friday afternoon where the 2023 stop began early on a Wednesday. The more than 2,500 cancellations counted by 6:30 p.m. were nearly double the 1,300-plus logged for the whole day in 2023, and the more than 10,500 delays had passed that day's roughly 10,000.
notknown_html:
The FAA has not said what caused the telecommunications outage. An airline source told CNN the problem began with network routers and spread nationwide, and CBS News reported that the affected system is operated by the contractor L3Harris, which had not responded to its request for comment. The FAA has confirmed neither account. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a threat to the country, and the FAA said it does not believe the outage was a cyberattack.

Three days before the stop, on Nov. 10, the FAA expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. Mullin said the administration is examining that rollout, according to Fox News, and no official has connected the tool to the stop or reported a link so far.

This story reflects what was known at 7:06 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, 2026. We will update the end time, the cause and the final delay counts as the FAA and flight trackers report them.
